HTTPay charge-then-401 pattern: the x402 probe returns 402 (looks payable) but after you PAY the gateway returns HTTP 401 'Service \'resend\' requires authentication' and instructs you to pass your own upstream Resend API key via the X-Upstream-Token header
No email is actually sent without your own Resend bearer key — unusable for keyless agents
Money is lost on the call ($0.001) even though it 401s — do NOT retry
Violates MasterKey no-API-key policy; should be dropped/excluded from the registry
usage.guide: Do not use this endpoint. Although the x402 preflight shows 402/payable, the HTTPay gateway charges you and then returns 401 requiring your own Resend API key via the X-Upstream-Token header. No email is sent without that upstream key, so it is unusable for a keyless agent and should be excluded from the registry.
